newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PARLIAMENT BEGINS DEBATE ON 1997 BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PARLIAMENT BEGINS DEBATE ON 1997 BUDGET.

text.p: The lower house of Czech parliament has begun debate on the third and final reading of the government's draft 1997 budget, with a final vote expected later on Friday.

After an agreement of the three coalition parties to support the budget on Thursday, the minority government needs two opposition votes to assure approval of the planned balanced budget of 549.1 billion crowns, up from 491 billion in 1996.

The house will vote on a total of 23 line-item amendments to the budget plan followed by a final vote on the whole package. Members said that they expected the final vote to be reached by Friday afternoon or in the evening.
In October four members of the opposition Social Democrats broke party ranks to allow the draft 1997 budget to get through the parliament's first reading.
The balanced budget total was locked in by virtue of its approval in the first reading, although amendments to line items can be made with balancing cuts or addition elsewhere in the account.
Observers widely expect the budget to be approved, as there are no signs that the opposition deputies have dropped their support, although the margin still would be very narrow.

On Thursday coalition leaders said they had reached a compromise after a junior partner, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), demanded a commitment to a deregulation plan on energy and housing rents and tax cuts.
The three party leaders agreed to appease ODA by completing the deregulations and tax cut schedule by the year 2000, the end of the government's current term.
